# Website review

Use this template for source reviews, project-stage reviews, and "what should happen next" assessments.

This template's wrapper is mandatory: keep the frontmatter, make sure it opens and closes correctly, keep the single `#` heading, place `---` before every main section after the first, and end the document with a final `---`.

---

## Confirmed context

- Summarise the project type, stage, and the most important confirmed facts.
- Keep this section factual.
- Distinguish confirmed inputs from assumptions.

---

## Missing intake

- List the missing source material, decisions, approvals, or strategic inputs that still matter.
- Group related gaps together.
- Keep the list focused on what materially affects the next step.

---

## Working defaults for now

- State any reasonable working assumptions being used temporarily.
- Label them clearly as defaults, not confirmed facts.
- Omit this section if no working defaults are needed.

---

## Recommended workflow

- Name the single most appropriate next workflow only in plain editorial language.
- Do not use internal workflow names, skill names, routing labels, or hyphenated internal identifiers unless the user explicitly asks for the exact label.
- Explain briefly why this is the right next move now.
- If a later handoff is obvious, include it briefly at the end of this section.

---

## Best next step

- End with one clear next step only.
- Use plain-language action wording.
- Do not use internal workflow names, skill names, routing labels, or hyphenated internal identifiers unless the user explicitly asks for the exact label.
- Avoid listing several competing follow-ups.

---
